name: Laser comb
lead: A laser comb is a handheld device with teeth that part the hair while emitting low-power red laser light onto the scalp. It was among the first home light-therapy devices cleared by the FDA for androgenetic alopecia and is the lower-cost alternative to a full laser cap.

Users pass it slowly over the thinning areas several times a week. Because coverage is manual and sessions are longer than with a cap, results depend heavily on technique and discipline, and it is generally viewed as slightly less convenient for the same modest benefit.

paras: Like the cap, the comb delivers low-level red light to the scalp, where photobiomodulation is believed to stimulate follicle cells, support the anagen phase and reduce inflammation. The comb's teeth push hair aside so light reaches the skin, but any area the user misses receives no dose.

Safety is good, with occasional mild scalp irritation or dryness. Evidence is the same body of sham-controlled trials covering combs, caps and helmets, which shows a moderate average density gain but with small samples, short follow-up and industry involvement. Gains are partial, need continuous use, and are inferior to approved drugs, so the comb is best seen as an add-on.
